slides.title: Power Converters - Overview o Although the conventional motor vehicle is well over a century old and was once exclusivel
slides.body:
exclusively powered by heavy mechanical systems, it has evolved with the advent of
power electronics (PE). Today, power electronics are incorporated at various levels
within all automobiles.
o In EVs, power electronics is the brain of the powertrain system . It controls the
electric motor and provides the connection to the high-voltage battery. To operate a
motor, it is necessary to transfer energy from onboard source(s) to the motor. This
energy needs to be transformed in a controlled manner, to create a rotating magnetic
field in order to match the load requirements. All these phases (transfer,
transformation, and control) are enabled by the power electronic systems.

slides.title: Power Electronics – Definition and applications
slides.body:
Power Electronics deals with the use of electronics for converting and
controlling the flow of electrical energy from the source to the load in the
most efficient way (“power processing”).
Some automotive applications:
o Electric traction inverters (hybrid and battery-electric drive trains)
o Power management (DC-DC converters, body electronic and auxiliary
drives)
o Electrical power steering (EPS)
o Medium-voltage high-power electronics/48V electronics
o Thermal management for power electronics
o Electric vehicle charging

slides.title: DC Machine - Converters
slides.body:
For DC motors, the choice of converter is
primarily dictated by the nature of the power
source. If this source is alternating current the
converters used will be rectifiers that work with
natural switching devices, while, if the source is
direct current, choppers that are made with
forced switching devices are used.
So, the power electronic topologies employed to
drive a DC machine are:
o AC/DC rectifier
o DC/DC chopper

slides.title: AC/DC rectifier - Classification
Single-phase half-wave rectifier
slides.body:
This solution is currently used for machines with a power
of just over 20 hp, therefore suitable for light traction.
This d.c. drive is very simple, needs only one power
switch and one freewheeling diode connected across the
motor terminals for the purpose of dissipation of energy
stored in the inductance of the motor and to provide an
alternative path for the motor current to allow the power
switch to commutate easily.
However this converter results in poor motor
performance.

slides.title: Single-phase full-wave half-controlled rectifier
slides.body:
During the positive half wave T 1 and D 2 are directly biased, and
conduction occurs after the command pulse is sent to the thyristor T 1.
The current flows in the motor through the two components.
The load is then effectively closed in short circuit, the diode D 2
progressively stops conducting and the current passes through the
flywheel diode as it represents the path with the lower resistance.
Then for ωt = π the current on T 1 goes to zero and the component
switches off. At this point, T 2 and D 1 start conducting. The current
conduction proceeds up to the inversion of the half-wave which causes
the flywheel diode to polarize again directly. Once the diode conduction is
finished, the cycle begins again.

slides.title: Single-phase full-wave fully-controlled rectifier
slides.body:
The choice of the converter implies the possibility of inverting the
supply voltage, but not the armature current, therefore it will be
possible to operate from motor in forward running and as reverse
braking (first and second quadrant).
During the positive half wave T 1 and T 3 are directly polarized and
conduct as soon as the gate pulse is sent to them. This conduction
lasts until, in correspondence with the negative half-wave and the
next gate pulse, T 2 and T 4 are commanded. The current is then
switched and passed to this pair of devices, simultaneously bringing
the previous pair of components to shutdown.

slides.title: Single-phase dual rectifier
slides.body:
DC motors may require to be operated in four quadrants without a switching changeover. A simple dual converter
drive which consists of two single-phase full bridge converters connected in inverse-parallel supplying a d.c motor is
used. One bridge for one direction of motor current and the other bridge for the opposite direction of current. The
controls are interlock to prevent their simultaneous operation to avoid short circuits on one another. Bridge-I provides
operation in the first and fourth quadrants while bridge-II provides operation in second and third quadrants .
This drive is employed for motors of rating up to 15 kW.

slides.title: Three-phase full-wave half-controlled rectifier
slides.body:
The three-phase semiconverter is a one-quadrant drive . Its circuit includes a freewheeling diode D FW to maintain
continuous load current. It uses three thyristors and three diodes; hence a cost advantage is obtained compared with the
full-converter. This converter is used for motor ratings from 15 to 150 hp. The components activation sequence is:
T1-D2,T2-D3,T3-D1
A voltage is found on the load which will consist of "pieces“ of the line-to-line voltages vAB, vBC, vCA and - vAB, - vBC, - vCA.

slides.title: Three-phase full-wave half-controlled rectifier
Three-phase full-wave fully-controlled rectifier
Three-phase dual rectifier
slides.body:
Four-quadrant operation of a medium and large size d.c. motor drive (200-2000 hp) can be obtained. The
average motor voltage is required to be equal for both converters, which implies that the firing angles of the
two sets of the thyristors should sum to 180˚.

slides.title: Chopper
slides.body:
A chopper is a static power electronic device that converts fixed DC input
voltage to a variable DC output voltage. It could be considered as DC
equivalent of an AC transformer since it behaves in an identical manner.
Chopper systems are characterized by:
- high efficiency;
- fast response;
- regeneration operation capability.
The power semiconductor devices which are employed in these circuits
can be force commutated thyristor, power BJT, MOSFET and IGBT. GTO
and MCT based choppers are also used. All these devices actually
operate like a switch.

slides.title: Chopper - Classification
slides.body:
Choppers can be classified as follows:
- Class A (step-down or buck) 🡪 I quadrant
- Class B (step-up or boost) 🡪 IV quadrant
- Class C (inverting or buck-boost or half-bridge) 🡪 I-IV quadrant
- Class D 🡪 I-II quadrant
- Class E 🡪 4 quadrant

slides.title: Chopper – Class A (step-down or buck)
slides.body:
The output voltage is always less than or at most
equal to the supply voltage.

slides.title: Chopper – Class B (step-up or boost)
slides.body:
The output voltage is greater than the input voltage
When the switch is turned on, the power supply supplies
energy to the inductance which accumulates it and there is a
growth of the current. The previously loaded capacity cannot be
discharged on the power supply due to the diode and is
discharged on the motor where the load current tends to
decrease due to the dissipative energy balance.
Subsequently, the switch is turned off and the energy
previously stored on the inductance is transferred onto the
capacity and the power source (but mainly on the capacity)
while the current on the power supply side therefore tends to
decrease.

slides.title: Chopper – Class C (inverting or buck-boost or half-bridge)
slides.body:
S1 D1 realizes the function of the buck chopper,
while the pair S2 D2 realizes the function of boost chopper.

slides.title: Chopper – Class D
slides.body:
- S1 and S2 in conduction, the voltage Va is equal to V;
(motor)
- S1 and D2 in conduction (S2 is off) and obviously Va = 0;
(recirculation)
- S2 and D1 in conduction (S1 is disabled) and also in this
case Va = 0; (recirculation)
- D1 and D2 in conduction (with S1 and S2 both off). (brake)

slides.title: Chopper – Class E (Full-bridge)
slides.body:
Motoring and regenerative braking in both EV forward
and backward operations are controlled electronically by
means of PWM, that is, by varying the duty cycle.
The four-quadrant DC chopper can offer the positive
armature voltage with bidirectional armature current and
also the negative armature voltage with bidirectional
armature current, hence achieving forward motoring
and forward regenerative braking as well as backward
motoring and backward regenerative braking.
